$comment: The modular monolith, declared.
Until this file existed the modules were folders: `services/export` and
`services/quality` each imported the other, `lib/` — documented as the layer
with no dependencies — imported from `services/` in seven files, and 76
imports reached past a module's `index.ts` into its internals. None of it
broke a rule, because there was no rule. Folders do not enforce anything;
this file plus `scripts/checkModuleBoundaries.mjs` do.
Three rules, all mechanical, all with a monotonic budget: today's count may
fall and must never rise. That is the same shape as `check:module-size` and
`check:any-budget`, and it works for the same reason — nobody has to agree
to a refactor before the bleeding stops.
1. LAYERS. A module may depend on its own layer or a lower one, never
upwards. `foundation` (lib, utils) is the bottom: it must not know that
`domain` exists. `domain` (services/*) must not know about `ui`.
2. CYCLES. Two modules that import each other are one module with twice
the surface, and neither can be read, tested or moved alone.
3. PUBLIC API. A module that declares an `api` is entered through it. An
import that reaches past `index.ts` into an internal file couples the
caller to a decision the module never published.
Las tres se aplican sobre un grafo, y de qué está hecho ese grafo es la
otra mitad de la garantía. Un módulo se declara por carpeta (`path`) o por
fichero (`files`), y lo segundo existe porque durante toda la vida de este
manifiesto los cinco ficheros de la raíz del repositorio —`types.ts` el
primero— quedaron fuera del grafo por no ser carpeta de nadie. Ver ADR-105.

modules.name: services (raíz)
modules.$comment: Not a module: the 19 loose files still sitting at the root of `services/`, matched last so the real modules win. They form cycles with eleven modules, which is why they are the largest number in the budget below. Each one that moves into a module lowers it.

modules.name: app
modules.$comment: A module may be declared by file instead of by folder, and these five entries are why. `App.tsx`, `index.tsx`, `types.ts`, `constants.ts` and `utils.ts` live at the root of the repository, so no prefix caught them and the gate never opened them — for its whole life. That is not a detail: `types.ts` is imported by 25 of the 34 modules and imports six, so it closes the graph on its own. Measuring the modular monolith without it produced a green gate over 27 mutually reachable modules. See ADR-105.

modules.name: types.ts
modules.$comment: Declared one by one rather than as a single `shared kernel` because each is fixed on its own and the budget has to be able to fall one at a time: `constants.ts` only imports types and is inert, `types.ts` is the knot (F3-07), and `utils.ts` is a file with a utility's name holding prompt composition (F3-08). `foundation` and not `domain` because the layer is decided by what sits below: `lib` imports them, so they are below `lib`. Calling them domain would have turned the finding into `lib imports domain`, naming the consumer instead of the cause.
